### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d47805ea4dd975fefb7c273ef28a9c0ab1112147` — the merge of head `f374e3ceba175f98b5f7c1440825063bce9e03df` into base `67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d47805ea4dd975fefb7c273ef28a9c0ab1112147 && git checkout d47805ea4dd975fefb7c273ef28a9c0ab1112147
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94 f374e3ceba175f98b5f7c1440825063bce9e03df && git checkout -B drift-repro 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94 && git merge --no-ff f374e3ceba175f98b5f7c1440825063bce9e03df

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

### ① Derived judgments

Ten moved answers, each checked against the tree.

1. Platform item (a package-less registry entry with no stored row) beside one or more enabled packages, on get and `/layers`: 200 to 409 naming every package and `platform`. Named `narrowing`: right. Matches ruling Q1.
2. A package-less item beside two or more enabled packages: the 409 gains one candidate (`environment` or `platform`). Named `narrowing (candidate added)`: acceptable; the status does not move.
3. In process, the refusal of `MetadataManager.get('action', NAME)` gains `environment`. Declared for every placement of the package-less item. **Wrong for one placement**: see ④ F1.
4. Case 3, plain read: no item to the enabled holder's item. Named `widening`: right.
5. Case 3, `/layers`: the disabled package's body to the enabled holder's. The PR table names it `narrowing (leak closed)`, the `Clause-②:` line lists it under widening. The two disagree (nit, F7).
6. Case 1, `/layers` beside the environment's item and one package: the package's item to the environment's. Declared. Holds for the judged answer only where the metadata service answers no code layer (F3).
7. `MetadataManager.get('action', NAME)` beside one package: written-last to the package-less slot. Declared.
8. `MetadataManager.get('action', NAME, P)`: written-last to P's own slot. Declared in the changeset and as a dev deviation. The PR table names it `narrowing`, the `Clause-②:` line widening (nit, F7). The same store read serves step 2 of `GET /meta/action/NAME?package=P`, so that face can move too where the service holds a package-less in-memory item on another object; that reach is not declared (F6).
9. Case 3, the route's declaration read on the enabled holder's object: none to the holder's. Declared.
10. Exports: `refuseActionHeldByPackages` gains an optional fourth argument; `judgeBareActionRead` and `PackagelessActionHolder` are new module exports. Neither package index re-exports the module, so no published surface moves.

Execution face kept on main's answer per seat ruling B. Measured in the diff: with a package-less registry entry present and `face === 'execution'`, `judgeBareActionRead` makes main's own call (`refuseActionHeldByPackages(host, name, objectLessRefused)`) and returns no answer, so step 3 reads `getItem` as on main. With no package-less entry, the one-enabled-holder branch applies to both faces; it differs from main's `getItem` only where a disabled package's item sits ahead of the enabled holder's (case 3, declared). 3 route pins hold this: case 1 platform variant, case 2 on two routes, case 3 on 3 shapes.

Exact reads: both judge call sites are guarded by `!request.packageId`, so the protocol's `?package=P` judge (`admitExactQualifier`, `exactQualifierItem`) is untouched.

List reads: no list path is in the diff; none moves.

### ② Semver level

Consistent. The changeset bumps `@objectstack/metadata` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `patch`, the two published packages the diff moves; the other two touched packages carry tests only. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write changes. Under the rule a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition; the changeset carries the banner, one `adr-0087: not-required` marker, both declaration lines, and the FROM to TO for both the REST and the in-process address. The arm on the PR body and the changeset agree (`yes (narrowing)`). `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` completed success.

The changeset's own wording inherits F1 ("whether the package-less item sits on the packages' own key or on another object") and names `/published` on three arms that carry no pin in this diff (F2).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation 1 (`get('action', NAME, P)` answers P's own slot first): answered. Declared in the changeset, pinned at the manager in both write orders. See F6, F7.
- Deviation 2 (execution face): answered by seat ruling B; the diff matches it (①).
- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Ruling Q1 (platform variant, 409): implemented on the protocol's get and `/layers`, pinned in 2 cases (1 at the protocol in the runtime file, 1 through the REST server). In process the store cannot tell the platform's item from the environment's: escalated, F4.
- Ruling Q2 / epic note 6798747403 (retire the stale entry): not implemented here, as the ruling allows. #32447 is not on `main` at this head (no commit of it in `81d404d8` or in `2359cead`), so the retire stays on carrier #32447, and the PR body says so. Pinned here: 1 case, a stale package-less registry entry with no composite holder while the service store holds two packages answers the store's 409. Measured beside it: where the registry itself holds the packages in composite slots, the stale entry (no row behind it) is classified `platform` and is named in the 409 as a holder. It never answers the read, but the refusal names a holder that no longer exists until the retire lands. Escalated to the seat: #32447 must carry the retire and this shape's pin.
- Ruling Q3 (case 3): implemented and pinned, 3 shapes on 2 reads plus REST.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (1): the core message says "held by N packages" when one candidate is the environment; reported with `carrier: none`. Not answered. Escalated: the seat files it or dismisses it in writing.
- `security_findings: withheld`: the content is not in the inputs. Escalated: the seat confirms it was routed.
- Consistency with #32533 (card #32352, removal counts holders by package): the read here counts the same way. A package-less slot is never a package holder, and both refuse at two packages. The hunks do not overlap (removal at `storeRemovalKeys`, read at `readStoreEntry`, `refuseAcrossOwners`, `readIdentity`), and neither changes a function the other calls. No semantic conflict in the count. Two differences for the seat to align: (a) the read's refusal now names the environment beside the two packages, #32533's removal refusal names the packages only; (b) with one package and an environment slot, the bare read answers the environment's item while a bare removal takes every slot of the name.

### ④ Design judgment

**F1 — must-fix. `package-slotted-store.ts`, `readIdentity`: the refusal omits the environment in one declared shape.** Two packages on one identity (both bind the name to the same object, or both object-less) and the environment's item on another identity. `readStoreEntry` asks each identity in turn; the shared identity refuses inside `readIdentity`, and the new branch adds `environment` only when `store.has(identity)`, the bare slot of that same identity. The environment's slot is under the other identity, so the refusal names 2 of 3 holders, as on `main`. `refuseAcrossOwners`, which would name it, is never reached. The changeset and the PR body declare this TO for every placement, and the epic's second red line is that a refusal names every candidate. The 2 store pins cover packages on two objects and all three on one key; this third shape has no pin. Fix in the store and pin it. The protocol's judge is not affected: it counts registry holders and names the package-less entry on any object.

**F2 — should-fix. `/published` is declared and not pinned.** The `Clause-②:` line and the changeset name `/published` on the platform arm (200 to 409) and the candidate-added arm. The diff's 21 new cases drive get and `/layers` only. The only `/published` pins in the REST file are #32244's two-package ones. The runtime dispatcher's doors are not driven by any new case either; the runtime file calls the protocol directly. Add a `/published` pin per declared arm, on both transports, or strike the face from the declaration.

**F3 — should-fix. `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`: the judged answer is the code layer only when the metadata service answers nothing.** The service read runs first and its answer is kept; the judged item is consulted in the `code === null` branch. With a service that holds the package's item (the artifact door's copy) and not the environment's, case 1's code layer stays the package's item, while the hunk's comment says the code layer is never a package's artifact beside the environment's own item. Every layered pin asserts `effective` only, in a harness whose row store answers no overlay row, so `effective` equals `code` there; none runs `/layers` over a real `MetadataManager`, and none asserts `code` or `overlay` apart. Pin `/layers` over the real service for case 1 and case 3, and make the comment say what the tree does.

**F4 — should-fix, needs a carrier. In process the platform's item is the environment's.** The store classifies every package-less slot as the environment's: beside one package it answers first, beside two it is named `environment`. The protocol refuses the same item as `platform` (ruling Q1). On `main` the store answered written-last, so this is no loosening, but the in-process read still picks where the rule refuses. The changeset says "the package-less item" in its body and "the environment's" in its `Clause-②:` line.

**F5 — should-fix. One CONTROL does not pin which holder answers, and the answer is not the rule's.** "The service's refusal naming a DISABLED package beside A and the environment is no refusal" asserts `toBeDefined()`. Read through the tree: the store refuses (two packages), `rethrowPackageScopedRefusal` now counts one enabled package and falls through, and step 3 serves the registry's judged holder, package A's item. The environment's item in the service store, beside one enabled package, does not answer first. The sibling case without the disabled package answers the environment's item. Pin the answer; if the split between the service store and the registry is out of this card, file it.

**F6 — should-fix. Two residues of the in-process env-first rule, both unchanged from `main` and both outside the pins.** (a) `MetadataManager.get` returns on an in-memory hit before the loaders' slots are read, so env-first holds only when both items are in one view; a package's in-memory slot beside an environment item held only by a loader answers the package's. (b) The P's-own-first read also feeds `GET /meta/action/NAME?package=P` at step 2, undeclared on that face (① item 8). Declare (b); file (a).

**F7 — nit.** The jsdoc of `refuseAcrossOwners` still says a package-less item beside one package's "answers as before", and `readStoreEntry`'s says a read naming none answers "the slot written last"; both are now the env-first rule. The manager pin's label reads "?package= is unchanged" on an answer the same PR moves. The PR table and the `Clause-②:` line give different arms to items 5 and 8 of ①.

Break attempts that held:
- Case 1, environment variant: the judge returns the registry's package-less entry only when an active package-less row binds the name to the same object (or none) and exactly one enabled package holds it; step 1 then serves the stored row as on `main`. Both registration orders and the object-less shape are pinned (2 cases).
- Case 1, platform variant: 409 with candidates in the order packages, then `platform`; the object-less judge's refusal is merged without a duplicate candidate.
- Case 2: 409 names both packages and the package-less holder on two objects and all object-less (protocol 2 cases, REST 1, store 2).
- Case 3: one enabled holder is served through `getPackageScopedItem`; a disabled package's composite or stamped bare-slot entry no longer answers. A package-less entry beside one enabled and one disabled package is judged beside the one enabled holder. Two CONTROLs keep the enabled-first and one-holder answers.
- No resolution loosens: every new branch either refuses where `main` served, serves the one enabled holder where `main` served none, or serves the environment's item where `main` served written-last. No first-registered fallback is added; `getItem`'s first-composite read is bypassed, not extended.
- Stale bare-slot entry: beside any enabled package holder it never answers as the environment's item (no row, so `platform`, refused). See ③ for the candidate it adds.
- `rethrowPackageScopedRefusal`: counting enabled packages alone cannot swallow a real refusal, because the judge has already refused two enabled registry holders before any layer is read. Its one side effect is F5.
